claims.claim: An essayist characterises J. Eric Holmes's Basic Set prose as dispassionate, methodical and encouraging.
claims.source: Serban Ionita, 'The Shadowed Old Gods of Game Design', The RPG Gazette, 2025
claims.quote: His prose is dispassionate, methodical, and encouraging

claims.claim: The same essay calls the original 1974 boxed set's text dense and peculiar.
claims.source: Serban Ionita, 'The Shadowed Old Gods of Game Design', The RPG Gazette, 2025
claims.quote: The text in the set was dense and peculiar

claims.claim: The same essay calls Tom Moldvay's 1981 Basic text both efficient and lyrical.
claims.source: Serban Ionita, 'The Shadowed Old Gods of Game Design', The RPG Gazette, 2025
claims.quote: Moldvay’s text seems both efficient and lyrical

claims.claim: The essay says Moldvay's adventures implied a cosmology, a history and a mood through their placement of statues, monsters and ruins.
claims.source: Serban Ionita, 'The Shadowed Old Gods of Game Design', The RPG Gazette, 2025
claims.quote: Each adventure implied a cosmology, a history, and a mood

claims.claim: The essay says Moldvay's adventures communicated worldviews rather than merely offering maps.
claims.source: Serban Ionita, 'The Shadowed Old Gods of Game Design', The RPG Gazette, 2025
claims.quote: These adventures communicated worldviews, rather than merely offering maps

claims.claim: The article says Gygax's settlement populations and locations followed real-world economic maxims.
claims.source: John Roy, 'Greyhawk Returns in the 2024 Dungeon Master's Guide', D&D Beyond, 2024
claims.quote: His settlement populations and locations followed real-world economic maxims

claims.claim: The article says Gygax gave each nation its imports, exports and the trade routes used to carry them.
claims.source: John Roy, 'Greyhawk Returns in the 2024 Dungeon Master's Guide', D&D Beyond, 2024
claims.quote: each nation's imports and exports and the trade routes they used

claims.claim: Zeb Cook says TSR's early module settings were held to no more than what would fit on a page.
claims.source: David 'Zeb' Cook, Kobold Press world building seminar transcript, part 1, 2025
claims.quote: We made no more than what we could put on a page
claims.page: first exchange on models of world building

claims.claim: Cook says every early TSR module required a quick setting created only so the module could be explained.
claims.source: David 'Zeb' Cook, Kobold Press world building seminar transcript, part 1, 2025
claims.quote: For every module, you had to create a quick setting
claims.page: first exchange on models of world building

claims.claim: Cook reports readers wrote in convinced TSR held much more setting material than the page contained.
claims.source: David 'Zeb' Cook, Kobold Press world building seminar transcript, part 1, 2025
claims.quote: You obviously have a whole bunch more
claims.page: first exchange on models of world building

claims.claim: Baur calls the Forgotten Realms the kitchen sink approach to world building.
claims.source: Wolfgang Baur, Kobold Press world building seminar transcript, part 1, 2025
claims.quote: The Forgotten Realms is the kitchen sink approach to world building

claims.claim: Baur describes a newer one-book model as providing the minimum viable world building.
claims.source: Wolfgang Baur, Kobold Press world building seminar transcript, part 1, 2025
claims.quote: to provide the minimum viable world building
claims.page: exchange on models of world building

claims.claim: Cook says the worst world building books he has read are literally just lists of places and people.
